totally new to actually setting up a wallet and buying Bitcoin. I understand how it works and know what it is. -Just looking for opinions on the best first wallet from some veterans. Seems coinable and a few others are the first to pop up on Googles search. Any insight would be awesome.
Whats the BEST first wallet for a noob? Coinbase?

Try going through Bitcoin.org's "Choose your wallet" page here: https://bitcoin.org/en/choose-your-wallet

Let me know if you have anymore questions!

Yeah, I think coinbase is probably the best for a first wallet. I'm partial to blockchain.info for it's ease of use, security model (hybrid online wallet) and potential for anonymity, but for just getting comfortable holding and using bitcoin it's hard to beat Coinbase.

Assuming you're getting your feet wet with a small amount, why not install a wallet on your phone? Much handier than an online wallet. No ID verification required, but you need to get your bitcoin somewhere like localbitcoins.com or the builtin mycelium local traders. I'd go with mycelium. Make sure you keep your HD seed written down in case you lose/damage the phone tho.

I like LocalBitcoin.com's wallet system. They provide you separate codes as a two-factor entry system, and they can change your public key address randomly every couple of weeks so your transactions can't be tracked easily on the blockchain. And you are a click away from moving your BTC into another currency. I would use them until you are ready for Case Wallet or Trezor
